target_customer: B2B sales and marketing teams with large lead databases (for example Randstad, General Assembly, Unit4)
problem: Sales reps lose or ignore leads that are not ready to buy. Saleswhale's AI assistant followed up by two-way email to qualify leads and hand over meetings.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, per seat early then enterprise pricing

founders.name: Ethan Le
founders.background_notes: Education and prior employers were not in any opened source.

investors: angel investors including Albert Ni and Royston Tay

technical_complexity.rationale: Natural language handling of email replies, CRM integrations and lead scoring; standard ML and integration engineering for the period, with NLP quality as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: CRM and marketing automation integrations created some lock-in but conversational email assistants had several rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Marketing automation vendors did not copy it in a documented way; 6sense acquired it in January 2022.

market_need_then: The company claimed over $1.5 million in pipeline and $130,000 in closed deals for dozens of customers between February and April 2017 (company claim reported by e27, unverified), and had over 100 customers by April 2019.

identity.logo: A whale, per the name (details not confirmed)

rebrands.why: Company blog says it rebranded to reflect progress since 2016 after a brand sprint in early 2018; the post returned HTTP 503 when opened, so this comes from a search snippet

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable, easy name, a company-run rebrand and multiple trade press articles, but no merch or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Saleswhale raised a $1.2 million seed in April 2017 and a $5.3 million Series A led by Monk's Hill in April 2019, moving from per-seat pricing near $39 to $99 to enterprise contracts above $1,000 a month. It was acquired by 6sense in January 2022 on undisclosed terms and was described as the first YC-backed Singapore company to be acquired. The path looks like steady growth to a strategic acquisition rather than a breakout.
